# [Baseline] - MAC - D - Software Updates

How and when macOS downloads and installs its own updates.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | macOS |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Settings Catalog |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | own baseline — declarative software policy (DDM); extended with Software Update Enforce Latest and beta off from OpenIntuneBaseline macOS v2.0 beta (SC - Updates - D - Update Configuration) and microsoft/intune-my-macs (pol-sys-103, pol-sys-106), with its own deadline; CIS Apple macOS 26.0 Tahoe Benchmark v1.1.0 L1 1.1–1.6 |
| File | [`Baseline_MAC_D_Software_Updates.json`](Baseline_MAC_D_Software_Updates.json) |

> Declarative variant (DDM) instead of the com.apple.softwareupdate settings that OpenIntuneBaseline v1.0 provides. Deferral: 7 days for minor updates, 14 for major, 21 for system updates; Rapid Security Responses (Background Security Improvements) on, including rollback by the user (Apple default, lets a broken update be undone without IT); notifications on; standard users may install an OS update themselves. The three automatic actions are set to AlwaysOn (`_1`); until September 2026 they were set to `_0` (Allowed), and then nothing was enforced.
>
> **Enforce Latest (September 2026).** Delay in Days 30, Install Time 12:30. Microsoft: the delay counts from the release date of the update (or the creation of the policy) and 'only determines the target enforcement date and not the date that the update is offered to users'. 30 is deliberately larger than any deferral above (7/14/21): with OIB's 3 days the deadline would fall before a major update becomes visible through the 14-day deferral. 30 days is also the CIS limit (1.1, 1.6) and the maximum of the setting. 12:30 because a Mac is on during the day; at night it sleeps and only installs when opened. Enforce Latest enforces the newest version for that model, **including a new major version**: macOS 27 becomes visible 14 days after release and is enforced after 30 days. If a customer wants to release major versions themselves, remove this group and use a policy with a target version. Microsoft Learn: 'When an update enforcement is assigned, the device ignores software update settings, including automatic update actions' — as long as a deadline is open, it determines the behaviour; the automatic actions apply outside of that.
>
> **Beta** (softwareupdate_beta ProgramEnrollment AlwaysOff): no AppleSeed/beta builds on corporate Macs; macOS 15.4+, supervised.
>
> **App updates and configuration data** via two keys from the classic com.apple.SoftwareUpdate payload (AutomaticallyInstallAppUpdates, ConfigDataInstall), because the DDM declaration has no counterpart for them — mSCP (branch tahoe) also maps exactly these two CIS rules only to the profile keys. Both are already on by default in macOS; the policy makes them no longer switchable off. The other keys from that payload are deliberately not set, because DDM covers them.
>
> Open point: whether SystemPeriodInDays (21) also delays XProtect and configuration data is not defined in Apple's schema. If it turns out to do so, lower it.
